key_insight: An LLM can directly write effective variational quantum circuit parameters without optimizer feedback when the parameter space has interpretable structure.
engineering_relevance: LLM-written parameters could reduce repeated quantum-device evaluations, either as direct solutions or as strong optimization warm starts.
method: Provide the LLM with the problem, circuit, and gate conventions.
Execute its proposed angles without returning loss, gradient, or accuracy feedback.
Compare against random weights, classical optimization, and optimization initialized with LLM weights on the same circuit.
evidence_signal: Across 139 requests spanning digit classification, VQE, and MaxCut QAOA, LLM weights achieved 93–96% accuracy on digits 3 versus 8, while warm-started optimization reached its best value after a median of one evaluation.
watch_item: Reliability depends on parameter interpretability and gate conventions: fixed classification circuits above 30 weights fell to chance, and 6 of 42 QAOA replies used incorrect mixing-angle signs.
paper_title: Weight-Space Programming of Variational Quantum Circuits: Large Language Models Write Quantum Circuit Parameters Without an Optimizer
